puzzles.description: Dial in the espresso — adjust grind/dose/yield, pull a shot, hit 25-30s

feedback.fast: ⚡ Sour & thin. Too fast — grind finer.
feedback.slow: 🐌 Bitter & ashy. Too slow — grind coarser.

config.managerNote:
Sour/fast? Grind finer (↑). Bitter/slow? Grind coarser (↓).
Dose: keep it mid-range — 5 is our sweet spot.
Yield: short keeps it punchy — try 4.
Sweet spot is 25-26s. Not a second more. — M

hints: Read the Manager's note. Sour means too fast — grind finer (higher number).
Dose 5, Yield 4. Now adjust grind until you hit 25-26 seconds.
Grind 6, Dose 5, Yield 4 = ~25.8 seconds.

puzzles.description: 10-step number deduction — cups and shots don't add up

steps.narrative: You grab a tub and start clearing. Most tables are clean. You bring everything to the wash basin and count twice.
steps.prompt: Hot cups: 15. Cold cups: 6. Total in wash?

steps.narrative: But wait — in the corner. A table you don't remember serving. Four cups. Still slightly warm. Names written in handwriting that isn't yours:
steps.prompt: Total cups used today (wash + corner table)?

steps.narrative: You check the POS. 17 transactions. $89 total. Cash matches perfectly. No discrepancy in the money.
steps.prompt: Cups unaccounted for by sales (total used − POS transactions)?

steps.narrative: Think about the 21 cups in the wash. Those were used DURING service. The 4 on the corner table appeared AFTER. So of the 21 washed cups...
steps.prompt: How many of the 21 washed cups were from YOUR 17 sales?
steps.hint: You sold 17 drinks. Those cups went in the wash.

steps.narrative: 17 of the 21 washed cups are yours. That leaves cups in the wash that you did NOT serve:
4 mystery cups in the wash — served DURING the rush, but not by you. Plus 4 cups on the corner table — served to people you never saw. The cash is perfect. Nothing was stolen.
steps.prompt: Total drinks NOT made by you?

steps.narrative: You walk to the espresso machine. You zeroed the shot counter this morning. You check it now:
steps.prompt: You count the order tickets — coffee drinks only: 3 Lattes + 3 Caps + 1 Flat White + 2 Long Blacks + 1 Mocha + 1 Iced Latte + 2 Iced Long Blacks. Shots from orders?

steps.narrative: 13 shots from orders. But you also pulled a calibration shot this morning when dialing in the grinder. So accounted shots:
The 4 mystery cups in the wash — if those were coffee drinks, someone pulled shots for them too.
The machine says 21. You can account for 18. That leaves shots pulled by someone — behind you — that don't match ANY cup in the wash or on the tables.

hints: Start with what you can count: cups in the wash, cups on the table.
The POS says 17 sold. But 25 cups were used. The difference is the mystery.
Final step: Machine says 21 shots. You account for 18. The gap is 3.

puzzles.description: 5-step deduction — shelf tap, timeline, card elimination, number input, conclusion

steps.narrative: You walk into the store room to do the final stocktake. You check the rinse sink — three empty milk jugs. But wait... you remember this morning clearly. Tap the jugs you took from the shelf:
Jug C is empty and rinsed. Same batch as the others — it was right there on the shelf. But you only took 2.
steps.prompt: Jug A emptied by 8:15am. Jug B lasted until 9:30am. Rush ended at 10am. When was Jug C needed?
wrong: You had Jug A still going before the rush.
After the rush there were no more milk drinks to make.

steps.narrative: Jug C was fetched from the store room DURING the rush. The store room is behind a coded door.
steps.prompt: Who could have done this? Tap to flip and eliminate.

suspects.name: A customer
suspects.reason: No store room code. Counter blocks access.

suspects.name: You (forgot)
suspects.reason: Both hands full at the machine the entire rush.

suspects.name: Someone with the code
suspects.reason: Knows the layout. Has access. Knows where the milk is.

steps.narrative: Someone with access fetched a third jug during the rush. A full jug is 2L — enough for about 8 steamed milk drinks. The jug is completely empty.
steps.prompt: The 4 mystery cups in the wash were milk drinks. The 4 cups on the corner table also had milk. Total milk drinks from Jug C?

steps.narrative: A third jug. Fetched during the rush. By someone with the code. Used to make 8 drinks you didn't make. Rinsed and left in the sink — like someone who knows the closing routine.
steps.prompt: What does the third jug prove?
options: Someone worked a full shift beside you — setup to close
wrong: The jug is empty AND rinsed. That's not 'briefly.'
The jug was used DURING the rush, not after.

hints: You took 2 jugs this morning. The third is Batch C-3 — you saw it on the shelf.
Only someone with the store room code could get Jug C. Not a customer, not a driver.
4 mystery cups during rush + 4 cups on corner table = 8 drinks from Jug C.

puzzles.description: 4-step realization cascade — each correct answer lights up a cup

steps.question: Do you recognize these names?
wrong: You've never seen these names in the booking system.
No one on the roster has these names.
The handwriting is deliberate. These names mean something.
steps.after: Simon Peter. Thomas. Nathanael. James, son of Zebedee. Disciples.

steps.question: These four were all present at the same event. What connects them?
wrong: All twelve were at the Last Supper — but these four are singled out together in only one passage.
Thousands were there. These four are named specifically together elsewhere.
Only Peter walked on water. These four are named together in a different story.
steps.after: John 21. After the resurrection. A morning by the Sea of Tiberias.

steps.question: What happened that morning?
options: They caught nothing all night — then He told them to cast on the right side
He walked across the water to them
He sent them out to preach
wrong: That was a different night, a different sea.
That was earlier, during His ministry.
steps.after: They obeyed. The net filled. 153 fish. And when they reached the shore...

steps.question: What was waiting for them on the shore?
options: Breakfast — bread and fish on a charcoal fire
wrong: He was there. He'd been there the whole time.

onComplete.subtext: This isn't just a café. This is the shore.

hints: These aren't random names. They're from John chapter 21.
John 21:2 lists who was there: Simon Peter, Thomas, Nathanael, the sons of Zebedee...
Disciples → Breakfast on shore → Cast on right side → Bread and fish on charcoal fire.
